newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on FOMC woes, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on FOMC woes, profit-taking.

text.p: The Mexican bourse closed mixed on Thursday after zizagging through the session on changing fortunes on Wall Street and jitters ahead of the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates, analysts and traders said.
"It looks very cautious ahead of the FOMC meeting and I think the majority are calling each other's bluff," an analyst said, who asked not to be named.
The leading IPC share index ended down 7.00 points, or 0.18 percent, at 3,887.20.
The analyst added that first-quarter public finance data released mid-morning failed to produce a lasting recovery in share prices.
"The market did not react as expected to the economic data," he said.
Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz unveiled the Mexico's public finance balance sheet for the first quarter. Among other data, he said Mexico posted a public sector surplus of 8.991 billion pesos.
Ortiz told journalists separately he expected that first quarter GDP growth was between 4.5 and 5.0 percent.
A Reuters survey MEX22 of Mexico City financial houses shows an average forecast increase of 5.12 percent for first quarter GDP, which is due to be announced next Monday, May 19.
Dealers said share prices fell for much of the day due to profit-taking.
"There was a lot of profit-taking every time the Dow went down," a floor trader said. "But they are also taking fright befote the FOMC meeting."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average meanwhile ended up 47.39 points at a record close of 7,333.55.

"Several are bailing out at these levels to sit on the sidelines until after the FOMC meeting, but few want to buy at current prices for the same reason, so dealing was a little slow," another floor trader said.
Trading volume was much reduced from Wednesday's session at 77.2 million shares.
Traders drew attention to the strong performance by Mexico's three biggest financial groups, Bancomer, Banacci and Serfin, which all shrugged the downtrend among blue chips.
One trader suggested the three banks all creditors of Grupo Sidek, benefitted from speculation the troubled conglomerate has reached a deal to restructure its debt.
"The word is they'll pay off all their debt, I don't know where they'll get the cash from ... anyway, that would help their creditor banks," another floor trader said.
Bancomer end up seven centavos at 2.91 pesos, Banacci climbed 28 centavos to 17.80 pesos, while Serfin gained five centavos to 2.55 pesos.
Grupo Sidek B shares meanwhile gained four centavos to 75 centavos.
"Sidek will hold a shareholders' assembly on May 30, and that is why the stock is heating up," an analyst said.
Dealers said that after Bancomer, Telmex weighed most on the downside, off two centavos to 17.14 pesos.
Bancomer and Telmex accounted for almost 30 percent of all shares traded.
On the broad market, 110 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outstripped sliders by 47 to 40.
Dealers noted holding company Accelsa chalked up strong gains, gaining six centavos to 2.14 pesos, as in earluier sessions this week.
"Accel is a good small-cap stock, very cheap and sound fundamentals, that's why it is in demand,' a desk trader said.
(( --Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9562))
